instruction: In the student grades table, populate the 'Message' column (column F) with appropriate remarks for each student based on the grading scale shown above. Verify that Benedict, Blake, and Olivia have the correct remarks.

metadata.explanation: Task requires filling the Message column (F) with remarks based on the grading scale for ALL students in rows 10-15. Verified by: (1) checking all 6 students have non-empty Message values, (2) checking all values are valid remarks from the grading scale (Fail/Pass/Average/Good/Excellent), and (3) specifically verifying Benedict (row 10, 42 marks) has 'Pass', Blake (row 11, 94 marks) has 'Excellent', and Olivia (row 15, 67 marks) has 'Average'. Uses case-insensitive matching for robustness. Custom getter extracts all cells F10-F15, and custom metric performs comprehensive validation.

llm_judge_reasons: Instruction explicitly states 'Verify that Benedict, Blake, and Olivia have the correct remarks' - the verification requirement is scoped to these 3 specific students, not all students

Evaluator correctly verifies the 3 named students: F10 (Benedict: Pass), F11 (Blake: Excellent), F15 (Olivia: Average) with semantically correct expected values based on their marks (42, 94, 67 respectively)
Evaluator goes beyond minimum requirements by additionally checking: (1) all 6 cells F10-F15 are populated (all_cells_populated=true), and (2) all values are valid remarks from the grading scale list
Getter correctly extracts all cells F10-F15 from the Excel file using openpyxl with data_only=True to read computed values

Metric function correctly handles the 'type: rule' expected parameter - directly accesses expected.get('cell_values'), expected.get('all_cells_populated'), expected.get('valid_remarks') without incorrectly trying to access expected.get('rules')
Metric implements case-insensitive comparison (str(actual_val).strip().lower() == str(expected_val).strip().lower()) which is robust for categorical text values
Postconfig properly saves the file with Ctrl+S before verification, ensuring changes are persisted to disk before reading
Scoring logic is correct: checks specific values (3 checks), all cells populated (6 checks), all values valid (6 checks) = 15 total checks, returns passed_checks/total_checks
